blind_assessment.interpretation: No consistent superiority in prose/UI/headings demonstrated. X preferred only for capital-I differentiation in two diagnostic extremes; not a general reading preference.

ui.reason: Independent 16px labels, controls, dates and currency are readable with no obvious broken spacing; blind UI pairs show no robust difference.

headings.reason: 36px/500 Russian and English headings have coherent rhythm and open counters; no robust blind preference at 48px/500.

body.reason: Five-line English and Russian paragraphs at 16px/400 remain visually even and easily parsed at inspected scale.

sustained_reading.reason: An agent inspection of short passages cannot measure fatigue, reading speed, comprehension or long-duration comfort.

findings.specific: Blind diagnostic pairs 9 and 10: X capital I has horizontal terminals while Y presents a plainer vertical construction, reducing I/l distinction.
findings.recommendation: Preserve or evaluate differentiated capital-I treatment for identifiers and mixed alphanumeric UI; do not extrapolate this diagnostic preference to prose.
findings.acceptance_test: Compare I/l/1 strings at 12–16px across 400/500/700 and optical sizes 9/14/16, with randomized identity transcription by human participants.

findings.specific: Sustained-reading claim lacks direct evidence beyond short rendered paragraphs.
findings.recommendation: Keep long-form suitability provisional until a human reading evaluation.
findings.acceptance_test: Counterbalanced 10–15 minute Russian and English reading sessions with comprehension, error, preference and discomfort measures, against a specified reference at matched apparent size.

limits: Agent visual assessment, not human reading study.
